rules.rule: Give positions in solid businesses time; do not expect immediate moves.

sources.statement: Lack of patience is the worst trait; don't expect a position to move the moment you buy it.
Expect pullbacks along the way in a fast-rising small-cap or multibagger thesis and hold through them if the thesis holds.
Short-term prices can be irrational, but if the core business is solid the price will catch up.

rules.title: Buy longer-dated contracts to cut decay
rules.rule: Buy option contracts several months out rather than weeklies to reduce time decay.

sources.statement: Buy contracts at least 3-6 months out to reduce time decay; weeklies carry higher IV so you pay more for less time.
Buy LEAPS with about 1.5 years to expiration, and at least a year and three months.
Beginners should add two to four weeks to any contract or start with contracts three months to a year out.

rules.title: Buy quality below historical P/E
rules.rule: Buy quality stocks when their P/E is well below their historical average after a dip.

sources.statement: Treat a P/E that is low versus its industry as possible undervaluation, if earnings are not expected to fall.
Buy quality mega caps when their P/E is well below their own historical average and the stock is far off highs.
Buy beaten-down quality stocks after a dip on strong earnings when P/E compresses below its average.

rules.title: Buy stock instead of selling CSPs
rules.rule: If you want to own a stock, especially in a crushed market, buy it at your price rather than selling cash-secured puts.

sources.statement: If you truly want to own a stock, buy it instead of selling a cash-secured put on it.
Don't sell cash-secured puts to catch a falling knife in a crushed market; buy stocks at your price.

rules.title: Cap credit spread position size
rules.rule: Keep credit spreads to about 5% of the portfolio, since one loss can wipe out several winners.

sources.statement: Credit spread risk/reward is asymmetric against you; one bad trade can wipe out several good ones if not sized appropriately.
Keep credit spread positions generally within about 5% of the portfolio; start small and scale in.

rules.title: Filter divergences by oscillator extremes
rules.rule: Only count oscillator divergences that occur at extreme readings, such as RSI above 70 or a high percentile.

sources.statement: Only classify RSI bearish divergences when both RSI peaks form above 70.
Filter Awesome Oscillator divergences by percentile extremes (e.g., 90th percentile over 1000 bars).

rules.title: LEAPs only on strong companies
rules.rule: Use LEAP calls only on fundamentally strong companies with a clear upside reason that can recover from downturns.

sources.statement: Only open a LEAP call on a fundamentally strong company with long-term growth potential, an uptrend or strong momentum, and a clear reason it could move higher.
Trade LEAPS only on solid blue-chip stocks or SPY/QQQ, never on penny stocks.
Market downturns can make LEAPs expire worthless if the stock never recovers, so only use fundamentally strong companies you believe in long-term.
Prefer shares over LEAPS for a company you do not know well.

rules.title: Net premium flow at gamma levels
rules.rule: Confirm entries at put support, call resistance or the gamma flip with net premium flow turning your way.

sources.statement: Go with the flow: a long setup is confirmed when net drift turns bullish at put support; short when it rolls over at call resistance.
Favorite setup: pullback to the gamma flip point with positive net premium flow (A+++).

rules.title: Normalize features by volatility/scale
rules.rule: Normalize thresholds and features by ATR or percentages to remove scale and volatility bias.

sources.statement: Scale event thresholds by ATR so high-volatility periods don't dominate event counts.
Normalize features to remove scale (e.g., percentage MA slope instead of dollar slope; short/long ATR ratio for range expansion).

rules.title: Post-earnings announcement drift
rules.rule: After a big earnings-surprise gap, buy (or buy the gap test) and hold to capture post-earnings drift.

sources.statement: [Andrea Cimitan] Post-earnings announcement drift: after a positive earnings-surprise gap, buy and hold about 60 days to capture the persistent trend.

[Fabio Valentini] Earnings-surprise drift: after a big earnings-surprise gap, enter on the test of the gap with a stop below to capture the post-earnings drift (gap risk typically 2-4x smaller than drift).

rules.title: Prefer swing horizon
rules.rule: Favor multi-day swing holds where macro works and algos don't dominate, over intraday trading.

sources.statement: Use macro/fundamental analysis mainly for 2-4 day swing holds; it is less useful intraday and beyond a few days because conditions change.
As algos erode intraday edges, shift toward swing trading where you do not compete with high-speed algorithms.

rules.title: Recession/bear-bottom multiples
rules.rule: Size downside using recession earnings drops and multiple compression toward ~12-13x at bear-market bottoms.

sources.statement: In recessions earnings drop ~18% on average and the multiple compresses from a ~17x long-run average toward ~13x; use both to size downside.
Bear markets have historically bottomed around 11.9x earnings.

rules.title: Reversals need multiple confirmations
rules.rule: Trade reversals only with aligned signals such as momentum divergence, a structure break and a resistance zone, not on overbought readings alone.

sources.statement: Require strong momentum (e.g. bullish RSI divergence plus a break above the prior high) to confirm a reversal pattern; place the stop at the most recent low.
Do not trade reversals on overbought readings alone; require multiple aligned signals (resistance zone, channel boundary, RSI>70).

rules.title: Size pair legs by beta
rules.rule: Size pair-trade legs by relative beta, keeping the higher-beta leg smaller.

sources.statement: Paid source: statement withheld.
Paid source: statement withheld.

rules.title: Skip breakouts lacking stop or R:R
rules.rule: Skip direct breakouts without a sensible stop or attractive reward/risk, and wait patiently.

sources.statement: Skip direct breakouts when no sensible stop placement exists.
If a direct breakout lacks attractive reward/risk, be patient and wait.

rules.title: Wait for actual event outcomes
rules.rule: Ahead of uncertain events, avoid pre-set scenarios and wait for the actual numbers before deriving setups.

sources.statement: When outcomes are unclear, wait for the actual numbers before deriving setups.
Ahead of uncertain events (e.g., Jackson Hole) avoid pre-set scenarios; stay alert from the release time.

rules.title: Yield curve recession signal
rules.rule: Treat a flat yield curve and especially its un-inversion as recession signals.

sources.statement: Track the 2-year against the 10-year and treat a bear flattener toward inversion as an early recession and cycle-peak warning.
It is the un-inversion of the yield curve, not the inversion, that directly precedes recessions.
Treat a bear flattener, with short rates rising faster than long rates, as a cycle-peak warning, and do not wait for a crash to confirm the turn.
A flat yield curve (long and short yields nearly identical) is a recessionary signal.

rules.title: 1-5 day holds in competitions
rules.rule: In competitions, use 1-5 day swing holds rather than intraday trading to limit fees.

sources.statement: In competitions use 1-5 day swing holds rather than intraday because intraday is too costly in fees.

rules.title: 10-wide spreads for simple math
rules.rule: Use 10-wide call spreads to make the cost-versus-max-value asymmetry easy to evaluate.

sources.statement: Build a bull call spread by buying near the entry and selling a call about $10 higher, so risk is limited to the net premium.
Use 10-wide call spreads for simple asymmetry math (cost vs $10 max value).

rules.title: ATR plus VIX volatility filter
rules.rule: Use ATR with VIX to judge elevated volatility and adjust entry locations.

sources.statement: Use a 10-period simple daily ATR to gauge the current volatility regime.
Use ATR together with the VIX to judge whether volatility is elevated and adjust where you look for entries.

rules.title: Account for news slippage
rules.rule: Avoid trading the news spike; trade the directional information just after it, accounting for slippage.

sources.statement: Wait until the FOMC press conference ends before trading.
Account for slippage as the hidden risk of trading news; rather than trading the release spike, trade the directional information it gives just after.
After a data release, enter in the direction the data signal on a retracement rather than chasing the first move.

rules.title: Always have a bias
rules.rule: Show up with a market bias that price can change.

sources.statement: Always show up with a market bias; price can change your mind but trading without one gives a sub-50% hit rate.

rules.title: Automate mechanical strategies
rules.rule: Automate mechanical strategies so human deviations don't invalidate them.

sources.statement: Automate mechanical strategies; humans skip signals and move stops after losses, invalidating the tested system.
Automate the entry, stop loss, take profit and sizing so you cannot revenge trade or over-leverage.

rules.title: Avoid buying weeklies on Monday
rules.rule: Avoid buying weekly options on Monday, when uncertainty and premiums are highest.

sources.statement: Avoid buying weeklies on Monday; they are expensive because uncertainty is highest early in the week.

rules.title: Avoid directional bets at zero gamma
rules.rule: Avoid holding directional bets at zero gamma, which acts as a magnet.

sources.statement: Avoid holding a directional bet at zero gamma; it acts like a volume POC magnet.

rules.title: Avoid round-number stops
rules.rule: Avoid placing stops at round numbers where many traders cluster them.

sources.statement: Place stops a penny beyond the round number, not on the whole number.
Avoid placing stops at round numbers where many traders cluster them.

rules.title: Avoid self-created stress
rules.rule: Trade properly to avoid creating stressful situations for yourself.

sources.statement: Much stress in trading comes from creating hard situations for yourself; trading the right way is less stressful.

rules.title: Avoid strategy hopping
rules.rule: Stick with a plan that has an edge through losing periods while using stops.

sources.statement: Trade one consistent, repeatable process rather than improvising.
Avoid strategy hopping; if your plan has an edge, stick with it through losses while using stops.
Do not abandon a proven strategy during a normal drawdown.
Do not switch strategies while unprofitable, because switching resets your progress.

rules.title: Be flat overnight in competitions
rules.rule: In competition trading, hold from intraday to one day and stay flat overnight where possible.

sources.statement: In competition trading, hold intraday to one day and be flat overnight where possible.

rules.title: Beware decay in volatility products
rules.rule: Beware time decay when trading volatility products.

sources.statement: If trading volatility products, beware time decay.

rules.title: Bonds as information source
rules.rule: Use the bond market as an indicator rather than a trading vehicle if you cannot trade it well.

sources.statement: Use the bond market as an information source/indicator rather than a trading vehicle if you cannot trade it well.

rules.title: Bullish bonds at yield extremes
rules.rule: Turn bullish on long bonds when yields hit extremes.

sources.statement: Deploy cash when the 10-year yield peaks and rolls over.
Turn bullish on long bonds (TLT) when yields hit extremes.

rules.title: Buy AI infrastructure suppliers
rules.rule: Look past headline AI winners to power, cooling and network suppliers.

sources.statement: Look past the headline AI winners to the infrastructure suppliers: power, cooling and networks.
Buy the companies that own the current bottleneck in a buildout, the infrastructure that cannot be skipped or substituted.
Prefer bottlenecks that cannot be fixed quickly by building more capacity (power over chips).
Buy the suppliers collecting a spender's capex, not only the spender.
Look for overlooked resources a hot theme depends on while the crowd fights over the obvious winners.

rules.title: Buy ETFs in macro selloffs
rules.rule: In indiscriminate macro selloffs, buy broad-market ETFs.

sources.statement: During indiscriminate macro selloffs, buy broad-market ETFs to capture a market-wide discount without single-stock risk.

rules.title: Buy ITM call spread on crushed stock
rules.rule: When a stock is crushed and IV rises, buy an ITM call spread or sell an OTM put spread at support.

sources.statement: When a stock is crushed and IV rises, buy an ITM call spread (or sell an equivalent OTM put spread) at support.

rules.title: Buy back tested condor side
rules.rule: If one side of a condor is challenged, buy back the tested short strike and let the untested side expire.

sources.statement: If one side of the condor is challenged, buy back the tested short strike (cost up to the opening credit) and leave the untested side to expire.

rules.title: Buy mega-cap lawsuit fear
rules.rule: Treat lawsuit-driven fear in mega-caps as a buying opportunity.

sources.statement: Buy quality stocks after market overreactions to temporary bad news.
Lawsuits almost never make a dent in mega-cap companies; treat lawsuit-driven fear as a buying opportunity.

rules.title: Buy options after vol cools
rules.rule: Buy options when volatility has cooled, not when premium is inflated.

sources.statement: Buy option contracts cheaply, e.g., after volatility cools, rather than when premium is inflated.

rules.title: Buy straddle before big events
rules.rule: Before a pending big-move event, buy a short-dated straddle or strangle so only the move size matters.

sources.statement: Paid source: statement withheld.

rules.title: Buyback window bullish lean
rules.rule: Lean more bullish during buyback windows as one input, not a standalone signal.

sources.statement: Lean more bullish during corporate buyback windows and factor buyback seasonality into the overall analysis, not as a standalone signal.

rules.title: Cheap options aren't safer
rules.rule: Do not assume a cheaper option is safer than owning shares.

sources.statement: A cheaper option is not automatically safer than owning shares; lower upfront capital does not mean zero risk.
Avoid repeatedly buying cheap out-of-the-money options; time decay burns through the bankroll.

rules.title: Check strategy validity first
rules.rule: When results disappoint, examine the strategy's validity before blaming psychology.

sources.statement: If results disappoint, examine the strategy's validity before blaming psychology or risk management.

rules.title: Choose exposures before structure
rules.rule: Define direction, timeframe, conviction and vol level first, then pick the options structure.

sources.statement: Choose exposures first (direction, timeframe, conviction, vol level), then pick the structure; not the reverse.

rules.title: Close near-the-money shorts before expiry
rules.rule: Close or manage near-the-money short strikes into expiration to avoid pin and assignment risk.

sources.statement: Close or manage short strikes near the money into expiration to avoid pin risk/assignment turning defined risk into undefined risk.
Close spreads before expiration, especially when price is near the short strike, to avoid pin and assignment risk.

rules.title: Collar hedge for stock portfolio
rules.rule: Hedge a stock portfolio with an OTM SPY put financed by selling a further OTM call.

sources.statement: Hedge a stock portfolio with a collar: buy a 5% OTM 12-month SPY put and finance it by selling a ~10% OTM call.

rules.title: Combine FA, TA and risk management
rules.rule: Combine fundamental analysis, technical analysis and risk management in one process.

sources.statement: Combine fundamental analysis, technical analysis and risk management; removing any leg breaks the approach.

rules.title: Combine price, volume and structure
rules.rule: Combine price, volume and market structure to see where big money flows.

sources.statement: Combine price, volume and market structure to see where big money flows in and out.
Combine several indicators and act only when they agree.

rules.title: Compare to passive benchmark
rules.rule: Compare strategy results against a relevant passive benchmark.

sources.statement: Compare strategies with a relevant passive or risk-adjusted benchmark; making money is not enough if passive exposure did better.

rules.title: Concentration not a sell signal
rules.rule: Do not sell on concentration when leaders' earnings justify it.

sources.statement: In a concentrated bull market, be selective: own what actually drives it and ignore the rest.
Do not treat market concentration as a sell signal when leaders' earnings justify it.

rules.title: Convert QQQ gamma to NQ
rules.rule: Convert QQQ gamma strikes to NQ using the live NQ/QQQ ratio.

sources.statement: Convert QQQ gamma levels to NQ by multiplying strikes by the live NQ÷QQQ ratio and recalculate it live.

rules.title: Crash: stop covered calls, add convexity
rules.rule: When markets crash and vol spikes, stop selling calls and add long-vega convexity.

sources.statement: When markets crash and vol spikes, stop selling covered calls and add convexity (vega-sensitive longs) for the rebound.

rules.title: Credit spreads in ranges
rules.rule: Use credit spreads in range-bound markets.

sources.statement: Use credit spreads in range-bound markets as lower-risk, higher-probability trades.

rules.title: Credit/width PoP for spreads
rules.rule: Estimate credit spread PoP from credit-to-width, and favor 80%+ far-OTM spreads.

sources.statement: Estimate a credit spread's probability of profit from the credit-to-width ratio; favor far OTM spreads with 80%+ probability, 70% is borderline.

rules.title: Cross-correlation lead-lag
rules.rule: Use cross-correlation of log returns to detect lead-lag relationships between assets.

sources.statement: Cross-correlation of log returns can reveal lead-lag relationships between assets (positive k = A leads B).

rules.title: DCA needs quality assets
rules.rule: Choose quality businesses because DCA does not protect against declining ones.

sources.statement: DCA does not protect you from investing repeatedly into low-quality, declining businesses; what you buy matters as much as how often.

rules.title: Daily plus hourly swing charts
rules.rule: Use 1-3 years of daily candles for context and a 10-day hourly chart for entries.

sources.statement: Use daily candles over 1-3 years for range/volume context, then a 10-day hourly chart for focused swing entries.

rules.title: Death cross is lagging
rules.rule: Treat a death cross as lagging, so a bottom may already be near.

sources.statement: A death cross (50-day below 200-day) is a lagging signal, so a bottom may already be close.

rules.title: Develop with one contract first
rules.rule: Build the first strategy version with one contract and add sizing logic later.

sources.statement: Develop the first version with one contract; add position-sizing logic only in a second phase.

rules.title: Diagonals for earnings events
rules.rule: For earnings or event trades, consider a diagonal that combines term-structure, long-vega and directional bets.

sources.statement: For earnings/event trades, consider a diagonal: a term-structure bet, long-vega bet and directional bet in one.

rules.title: Discount limit when chasing missed move
rules.rule: When chasing a missed move, set a discounted limit entry and accept the lower fill probability.

sources.statement: When chasing a missed move, set a limit entry at a discount; the deeper the discount, the lower the fill probability.

rules.title: Divergence timing sensitivity
rules.rule: Distinguish timing-robust from timing-sensitive divergences, since laggy confirmation kills the sensitive ones.

sources.statement: Divergences are either timing-robust or timing-sensitive; laggy confirmation kills timing-sensitive ones.

rules.title: Dollar-cost average on schedule
rules.rule: Dollar-cost average in equal chunks on a fixed schedule.

sources.statement: Automate an affordable monthly saving rate, such as 10% of take-home pay, into a broad low-cost index fund and reinvest dividends.
Dollar-cost average in equal chunks on a fixed schedule to remove timing and emotional risk.
Buy the index sleeve on a fixed monthly schedule and never interrupt it; keep stock-picking timing out of that bucket.

rules.title: Don't add contracts with freed buying power
rules.rule: Do not add contracts when narrower condor wings free up buying power.

sources.statement: When narrowing condor wings frees buying power, do not add contracts; it re-increases gamma exposure.

rules.title: Don't buy-and-hold options
rules.rule: Do not hold options like stock since they decay toward worthless.

sources.statement: Options are designed to expire worthless; do not buy and hold them like stock.

rules.title: Don't fight the Fed
rules.rule: Read jobless claims and CPI to anticipate Fed rate direction and trade with it.

sources.statement: Don't fight the Fed: read labor (initial jobless claims) and inflation (CPI) to anticipate rate direction.
Expect the Fed to stay hawkish while the labor market is robust and inflation sticky, since it has a dual mandate.
Watch whether long-term inflation expectations unanchor; if they do, expect hikes rather than cuts.

rules.title: Don't roll deep ITM replacement calls
rules.rule: Do not roll deep ITM stock-replacement calls after rallies; let changing leverage rebalance automatically.

sources.statement: Don't roll deep ITM stock-replacement call strikes after rallies; falling leverage sells strength and rising leverage adds on weakness automatically.

rules.title: ES Tuesday-to-Wednesday day-of-week tendency
rules.rule: Study the ES tendency of buying the Tuesday open and exiting at the Wednesday open as a day-of-week effect.

sources.statement: Day-of-week test on ES: buying Tuesday open and exiting Wednesday open showed a baseline tendency worth studying.

rules.title: Enter when Fed changes direction
rules.rule: Position for a long trend when the Fed changes policy direction.

sources.statement: The best macro trade starts when the Fed changes direction; position for a long trend because the Fed keeps its new stance for several meetings.

rules.title: Exit fast on contrary news
rules.rule: When a news surprise contradicts your position, exit or hedge quickly during the market's digestion window.

sources.statement: [Jan Smolen] When a news surprise contradicts your position, use the market's slow digestion window to exit or hedge quickly instead of waiting.

rules.title: Exit when moves stop being impulsive
rules.rule: Exit when price action stops being impulsive and turns choppy.

sources.statement: Trade only impulsive moves; exit when price action stops being impulsive and avoid choppy sideways phases.

rules.title: Expect mean reversion of returns
rules.rule: After long above-average returns, expect more muted future returns.

sources.statement: After a long stretch of above-average returns, expect reversion to the mean with more muted future returns.
Expect very high returns to revert to the mean; treat about 20% a year as excellent.

rules.title: Fed cuts start late
rules.rule: Expect recession to have begun and cuts to be aggressive once the Fed starts cutting.

sources.statement: When the Fed starts cutting it is typically late and recession has basically begun; expect aggressive cuts.
Expect the worst equity declines after the Fed starts cutting rates, not while it is hiking.

rules.title: Fed delivers highly priced hikes
rules.rule: Assume the Fed delivers when a hike is priced at ~93%+.

sources.statement: When markets price a Fed hike at ~93%+, assume the Fed delivers (true since 2008).

rules.title: Fed more reliable than BoJ
rules.rule: Treat Fed signals as more reliable to trade than BoJ signals.

sources.statement: Treat the Fed as more credible/continuous than the Bank of Japan; BoJ signals are less reliable to trade.

rules.title: Fed pivot not guaranteed bullish
rules.rule: Do not assume a Fed pivot or lower rates guarantees a stock rally.

sources.statement: Do not assume a Fed pivot or lower rates guarantees a stock rally; the rate–equity relationship is not stable.

rules.title: Find your high-probability markets
rules.rule: Identify which markets and conditions give you higher probabilities.

sources.statement: Narrow trading to the instruments where your tracked results are best; his journal showed eight assets was not optimal, so he cut to ES, NQ and YM.
Find for yourself which markets and conditions give higher probabilities.

rules.title: Fixed routine and review hours
rules.rule: Fix a routine with set market-review hours and consistent sleep to reduce decisions and support discipline.

sources.statement: Fix a routine with set market-review hours and consistent sleep to reduce decisions and support discipline.

rules.title: Fundamentals where, technicals how
rules.rule: Use fundamentals to know where and when to look, and technicals for direction, entry, stop and target.

sources.statement: Use the chart only at the end of the process for execution, never as the reason for a trade; drivers come from fundamentals, intermarket and sentiment.
Use fundamentals to know where/when to look (scheduled catalysts like central bank releases) and technicals to decide direction, entry, stop and target.
Use technical analysis mainly to set cheaper limit-order entries for long-term buys, not as the basis of the trade.
Use fundamentals to decide what to buy and technicals to decide when to buy and sell.

rules.title: Harvest tax losses
rules.rule: Sell losing positions to harvest tax losses.

sources.statement: Harvest tax losses by selling positions at a loss for the tax benefit.

rules.title: High IV isn't directional
rules.rule: Read high IV as an expected big move in either direction, not upside.

sources.statement: High IV does not mean price will go up; it signals a big move in either direction.

rules.title: High IV premium is risky
rules.rule: Recognize that juicy premium in high IV comes with much higher risk.

sources.statement: When implied volatility is high, premium looks juicy but the risks are much higher.

rules.title: High win-probability threshold
rules.rule: Take only trades with roughly 70-80% estimated win probability.

sources.statement: Only take trades with roughly 70-80% estimated win probability so that edge decay of 10 points still leaves a profitable process.

rules.title: Hold bonds to rebalance into stocks
rules.rule: Hold bonds so you can sell them to buy stocks during a recession.

sources.statement: Hold bonds so they can be sold from a position of strength to buy stocks during a recession.

rules.title: ITM cash-secured puts capture drift
rules.rule: Consider striking cash-secured puts in the money to capture equity drift.

sources.statement: Consider striking cash-secured puts in the money (equivalent to slightly OTM covered calls) to capture equity drift.

rules.title: ITM for choppy, OTM for trending
rules.rule: Use ITM options for slow, choppy stocks and OTM options for fast-trending movers.

sources.statement: Use ITM options for slow, choppy stocks and short-term trades; use OTM options for fast-trending movers.

rules.title: IV is a dial, not switch
rules.rule: Adjust strikes and size to the IV environment rather than trading only in high IV.

sources.statement: Treat high IV as a dial not a switch: adjust strikes and sizing to the volatility environment rather than only trading in high IV.

rules.title: Implied vs expected realized movement
rules.rule: Sell defined-risk premium when you expect less movement than priced, and buy options when you expect more.

sources.statement: Compare implied movement with expected realized movement: sell defined-risk premium for contraction theses, buy calls/puts when movement beyond the priced range is expected.

rules.title: Inflation compresses P/E
rules.rule: Expect lower P/E multiples when inflation is higher.

sources.statement: Higher inflation means stocks should trade at cheaper P/E multiples — inflation is like gravity on stocks.

rules.title: Inflation reassessment threshold
rules.rule: Reassess the inflation leg if CPI/core PCE or Truflation stays above ~3%.

sources.statement: Reassess the inflation leg if CPI/core PCE stays above ~3% or Truflation above 3-3.2%.

rules.title: Inside-day buy-stop setup
rules.rule: At an important level, place a buy-stop above the inside-day candle with the stop below the 200-day MA.

sources.statement: Inside-day setup at an important level: buy-stop above the inside (baby) candle, stop-loss below the 200-day line.

rules.title: Jobless claims warning
rules.rule: Treat claims above a threshold for several weeks as a first labor-market warning.

sources.statement: Labor-market warning: weekly jobless claims above a threshold for several weeks is a first warning sign.

rules.title: KOSPI reversal lead
rules.rule: Use KOSPI reversals after consecutive down sessions as a lead for a US-open bounce.

sources.statement: Use KOSPI reversals after consecutive down sessions as a lead for a bounce at the US open.

rules.title: LEAP target at pre-crash high
rules.rule: Use the prior pre-crash high region as the profit target for recovery LEAP trades.

sources.statement: Use the prior pre-crash high region as the profit target for a recovery LEAP trade.

rules.title: Late speculative runs are fragile
rules.rule: Expect late speculative rallies to top on small doubts.

sources.statement: Recognize exhaustion at tops: a vertical move, euphoric headlines and everyone asking about it; check who is selling to the crowd.
Late speculative runs are fragile: after a big speculative rally, a small hawkish doubt can be enough to set the top.

rules.title: Learn with small real money
rules.rule: Learn new markets with small real money rather than demo accounts.

sources.statement: Learn new markets with real (small) money, not demo/simulated accounts; demo success does not transfer to real capital.

rules.title: Leveraged ETF decay
rules.rule: Account for volatility decay in leveraged ETFs.

sources.statement: Leveraged ETFs suffer volatility decay: losses compound more heavily than the underlying.
Do not hold leveraged ETFs long term; decay erodes them in choppy markets.
Use leveraged index ETFs only as short-term bounce trades, never as holds.
Judge growth by average return minus half the variance, not by the average return; volatility drag also erodes funds that reset leverage daily.
Do not hold a 3x leveraged index fund (such as SPXL) as a long-term position, because decay erodes it.

rules.title: Long deferred after front-month collapse
rules.rule: When a front-month commodity collapses, go long deferred contracts or producers instead.

sources.statement: When a front-month commodity collapses (e.g. storage glut), go long deferred contracts or producers instead of the front contract; low prices cure low prices.

rules.title: Long strangle flat risk
rules.rule: Remember a long strangle loses on both legs if the stock stays flat.

sources.statement: A long strangle loses on both legs if the stock stays flat.

rules.title: Long strangle leg management
rules.rule: On a long strangle, cash the winning leg gradually and exit the losing leg once the move resolves.

sources.statement: Paid source: statement withheld.

rules.title: Look for catalysts
rules.rule: For growth trades, seek catalysts such as earnings, launches or industry shifts.

sources.statement: For growth investing, look for events and catalysts such as earnings, product launches or industry shifts that can move the stock.

rules.title: Low VIX hurts systematic edges
rules.rule: Expect systematic edges to suffer when VIX is compressed below ~15.

sources.statement: Most trading systems work best in high volatility; when VIX is compressed (below ~15) systematic edges suffer.

rules.title: Macro as directional filter
rules.rule: Use macro as a long-term directional filter and trade in the conviction direction.

sources.statement: Read rates, liquidity and oil every week before making portfolio decisions.
Use macro as a long-term directional filter; you don't need to be early, just trade in the conviction direction.

rules.title: Macro conviction over 2-4 day horizon
rules.rule: Apply macro conviction over a roughly 2-4 day horizon to set intraday direction.

sources.statement: Macro conviction is most useful over a ~2-4 day horizon to set intraday direction; it reduces decision fatigue.

rules.title: Match R:R to trading style
rules.rule: Keep targets consistent with stop size and style; don't take day-trade profits on swing-trade risk.

sources.statement: Match exits to your style: do not take day-trader-sized profits on swing-trade risk (e.g. $5 stop with $15 target).

rules.title: Match long-delta structure to conviction
rules.rule: Use deep ITM calls for low conviction and low-delta OTM calls for extreme conviction.

sources.statement: Match long-delta structure to conviction: low conviction = deep ITM call stock replacement; extreme conviction = 10-20 delta calls.

rules.title: Mine academic papers for ideas
rules.rule: Use academic papers as a hypothesis source, extracting value rather than copying.

sources.statement: Academic papers are the best source of trading hypotheses; extract value rather than copying them.

rules.title: Minimum credit and exit on doubling
rules.rule: Set a minimum credit when selling spreads and reduce or exit if the spread doubles.

sources.statement: Paid source: statement withheld.

rules.title: Modular macro analysis
rules.rule: Use a modular analysis process, applying only the relevant blocks.

sources.statement: Use a modular process (geopolitics, liquidity, growth/inflation, sentiment, positioning, fundamentals, charts, risk); not every block is needed for every analysis.

rules.title: Need full option-buying pattern
rules.rule: Act only on a complete pattern of option buying, not on a single large print.

sources.statement: Do not read raw call volume or large prints near expiry as bullish; check the 25-delta risk reversal and whether trades hit the bid or the ask.
A single large option print is not a signal; you need the complete pattern of option buying before acting.

rules.title: Net drift premium flow
rules.rule: Use net premium flow drift as a read on bullish or bearish dealer hedging flow.

sources.statement: Use net drift (real-time net premium flow): rising positive = bullish dealer hedging flow; falling negative = bearish.

rules.title: Net drift unreliable around FOMC
rules.rule: Discount net drift signals around FOMC, because the market is pricing the event.

sources.statement: Net drift is less useful around FOMC because the market is pricing the event.

rules.title: Never stretch risk limits
rules.rule: Never stretch risk limits temporarily after a good P&L run.

sources.statement: Never stretch risk limits 'temporarily' after a good P&L run; overconfidence plus stretched limits precedes blowups.
Do not raise risk after a run of wins; he risked heavy after great trades and gave back all the gains and more.

rules.title: No fixed profit targets
rules.rule: Avoid fixed daily or monthly profit targets that force bad trades.

sources.statement: Avoid fixed daily or monthly profit targets; they act like a boss that forces bad trades.

rules.title: Non-linear theta decay
rules.rule: Remember that theta decay is non-linear and erodes static ATM long options to zero.

sources.statement: Theta decay is non-linear; an ATM long option that doesn't move decays to zero.

rules.title: One options position at a time
rules.rule: Beginners should open one well-researched options position at a time.

sources.statement: Beginners should open one options position at a time with a deep thesis instead of opening random contracts to collect premium, which blows up accounts.

rules.title: Overnight range breakout
rules.rule: Go long Nasdaq futures on a close above the 4-5 p.m. ET range in the first hour after reopen, with a 1:1 target, and exit by the European open.

sources.statement: [Matteo Conti] Overnight range breakout (Nasdaq futures): mark the 4-5 p.m. ET range; if a candle closes above it in the first hour after the 5 p.m. reopen, go long, stop at range low, 1:1 target, close by 3 a.m. CT European open.

rules.title: Own real assets in inflation
rules.rule: In persistent inflation, own stocks and hard assets over cash.

sources.statement: Against persistent inflation, go long real assets and energy and short long-duration bonds and weak sectors.
In a persistently inflationary regime, favor owning stocks and hard assets over cash.
Favor gold and other assets that cannot be printed when rates rise on government-debt fears rather than growth.
Treat gold weakness during high real yields as temporary when physical demand stays strong.

rules.title: PoP via breakeven delta
rules.rule: Approximate vertical spread probability of profit using the delta at the breakeven strike.

sources.statement: Approximate vertical call spread probability of profit using the delta of an option struck at the breakeven price.

rules.title: Pre-earnings run-ups shrink moves
rules.rule: Expect smaller post-earnings moves after big pre-earnings run-ups.

sources.statement: Do not buy ahead of an earnings print everyone expects to be great; when expectations are stretched, good news is not enough.
A big pre-earnings run-up usually means a smaller move after the report.
Expect stocks priced for perfection to sell off even on great reports, and do not buy their dips blindly.

rules.title: Prefer zones overlapping others' zones
rules.rule: Prefer zones that overlap other traders' approaches.

sources.statement: Prefer zones that overlap with other traders' zones/approaches; confluence raises the chance they hold.

rules.title: Price options probabilistically
rules.rule: Value options from probability-weighted payoffs, not the most likely price.

sources.statement: Price options from probability-weighted terminal payoffs, not by guessing the most likely stock price.

rules.title: Protect profits at exit
rules.rule: Judge trades by the exit and protect profits so winners don't become losers.

sources.statement: Paid source: statement withheld.
Take gains on a hype trade instead of holding out of stubbornness.

rules.title: Put credit spreads 1-3 weeks out
rules.rule: Choose put credit spread expirations about 1-3 weeks out for faster theta decay and adaptability.

sources.statement: Choose put credit spread expirations about 1-3 weeks out (ideally 1-2) to adapt quickly to news and capture faster theta decay.

rules.title: RSI 70/30 overbought/oversold
rules.rule: Use RSI above 70 as overbought and below 30 as oversold.

sources.statement: Use RSI to judge whether an index has moved too far too fast: above 70 overbought, below 30 oversold.

rules.title: RSI support bounce confirms uptrend
rules.rule: Confirm an intact uptrend by daily RSI bouncing around 55 and Bollinger Band shifts.

sources.statement: Paid source: statement withheld.

rules.title: Rebalance delta-neutral hedges
rules.rule: Rebalance delta-neutral hedges as delta changes.

sources.statement: Delta-neutral hedging must be rebalanced as delta changes; a long call at 0.5 delta is hedged by shorting 50 shares.

rules.title: Recession investing is defensive
rules.rule: In recessions aim to preserve capital, not get rich.

sources.statement: Investing during recessions is about keeping your head above water, not getting rich.

rules.title: Rent the winning hedge
rules.rule: If your hedge keeps beating your risk asset, allocate to the hedge rather than chase beta.

sources.statement: Paid source: statement withheld.

rules.title: Require multi-month data trends
rules.rule: Require several months of trend in data before drawing macro conclusions.

sources.statement: Require data to show a trend over several months before drawing macro conclusions.

rules.title: Research must reject strategies
rules.rule: Ensure your research process can reject losing strategies.

sources.statement: A research process must be able to say no; rejecting a losing strategy is money saved.

rules.title: Risk first, overlays last
rules.rule: Prioritize risk first, investing second and option overlays third.

sources.statement: Priority order: risk first, invest second, option overlays third.

rules.title: Risk reversal in targetless momentum
rules.rule: In strong momentum with no clear target, sell an OTM put at a level you'd own and buy an OTM call.

sources.statement: [Imre Gams] In strong momentum with no clear target, use a risk reversal: sell an OTM put at a level you'd happily own the underlying and use the premium to buy an OTM call.

rules.title: Risk-on vs safe-haven currencies
rules.rule: Buy growth currencies in optimism and JPY/CHF/USD as safe havens.

sources.statement: Expect pressure on risk assets when the dollar breaks out on a hawkish Fed; a hot economy plus hot inflation keeps the Fed hawkish.
Expect growth/commodity currencies (AUD, NZD, CAD) to be bought when markets are optimistic about global growth; JPY, CHF, USD are safe havens.

rules.title: Roll calls at 60-70 delta
rules.rule: Buy ~40-delta calls and sell or roll them when they reach 60-70 delta.

sources.statement: Buy ~40-delta calls (40-60 delta has highest gamma); when the call reaches 60-70 delta, sell or roll strikes.

rules.title: Rolling doesn't erase losses
rules.rule: Recognize that rolling a tested short option does not erase the loss already incurred.

sources.statement: Rolling a tested short option changes exposure and cash flows but doesn't erase the loss already incurred.

rules.title: S&P favors mean reversion
rules.rule: Use mean-reversion rather than breakout logic on the S&P 500.

sources.statement: Match logic to the instrument: S&P 500 rewards mean-reversion systems more than trend-following breakouts.

rules.title: S&P/gold ratio risk warning
rules.rule: Treat a monthly S&P/gold close below a key level with negative slope as elevated equity risk.

sources.statement: A monthly close of the S&P 500/gold ratio below a key level with negative slope signals elevated equity risk during the year (not an immediate trigger).

rules.title: SMA trend scorecard
rules.rule: Score trend -3 to +3 from the 20/50 SMAs and their slopes, and set exposure accordingly.

sources.statement: Score trend from -3 to +3: +2 above both 20/50 SMAs (+1 above 20 only), +1 if both slope up; mirror for bearish. Go mostly long at +3, hedge at +1/0, play downside when bearish.

rules.title: Sample at information-bearing events
rules.rule: Sample observations at information-bearing events rather than forecasting every candle.

sources.statement: Sample observations at information-bearing events (breakouts, sweeps, gaps, volatility changes) rather than forecasting every candle.

rules.title: Seek edges in under-covered stocks
rules.rule: Look for edges in small/mid caps with low institutional coverage.

sources.statement: [Matteo Conti] Look for edges in small/mid caps with low institutional coverage rather than heavily traded S&P/Nasdaq futures.

rules.title: Short-dated directional needs timing
rules.rule: Recognize that short-dated directional options need correct direction, magnitude and timing to profit.

sources.statement: Paid source: statement withheld.

rules.title: Size options from underlying stop
rules.rule: Size options by the projected delta-based loss at the underlying stop.

sources.statement: Size options from the underlying stop: average starting delta with projected delta at the stop, times move and multiplier, then divide the dollar risk by that loss.

rules.title: Size so stops are emotionally neutral
rules.rule: Size so that no single day's stop or profit changes your life emotionally.

sources.statement: [Fabio Valentini] Size so that no single day's stop or profit can change your life; feeling fear or excitement on a stop means you are oversizing.
Size tactical trades small enough that being wrong costs you almost nothing.
If raising risk makes you break rules or act emotionally, stop and go back down to the previous risk immediately.

rules.title: Size stock replacement by option leverage
rules.rule: Size deep ITM calls by option leverage, not like shares.

sources.statement: Size deep ITM calls by option leverage (delta x stock price / option price), not like shares.

rules.title: Skip earnings priced at ~2 SD
rules.rule: Skip an earnings trade if options already price in about two standard deviations of movement.

sources.statement: Skip an earnings trade if the options already price in about two standard deviations of movement.

rules.title: Sold puts carry crash risk
rules.rule: Remember sector crashes can drag quality names down 50%+, exposing sold puts.

sources.statement: Sector-wide crashes can drag even high-quality names down 50% or more, so sold puts are exposed to broad market risk.

rules.title: Stand down on volatile earnings condor
rules.rule: Skip an earnings condor if volatile activity shows into the close.

sources.statement: Paid source: statement withheld.

rules.title: Straddle prices earnings move
rules.rule: Estimate the priced-in earnings move from the ATM straddle price.

sources.statement: Estimate the priced-in earnings move by adding the at-the-money call and put prices (the straddle).

rules.title: Strike distance scales with time
rules.rule: Go further OTM only with more time to expiration; keep strikes near the money when time is short.

sources.statement: With more time you can go further out of the money; with less time keep strikes close to the money.

rules.title: Systems decay from amplitude change
rules.rule: Monitor move amplitude and intraday persistence as the cause of system breakdown.

sources.statement: Systems break not because direction changes but because move amplitude and intraday directional persistence change.

rules.title: TA guides through macro noise
rules.rule: Use technical analysis as the objective guide through macro noise.

sources.statement: Paid source: statement withheld.
Manage the portfolio off price action and positioning, not headlines; by the time a headline hits you are late.
Go long or short only on what the candlesticks show, not on geopolitical events or what politicians say.

rules.title: Tech vs S&P P/E convergence
rules.rule: Treat tech leaders as discounted when their forward P/E converges with the S&P 500's.

sources.statement: When tech's forward P/E converges with the S&P 500's, treat leaders as discounted because they historically trade at a premium.

rules.title: Time options from underlying structure
rules.rule: Time directional option entries from the underlying's price structure, using option flow only as confirmation.

sources.statement: Express a recovery with a defined-risk bull call spread only after price confirmation.
Time directional option entries from underlying price structure; use option flow and premium response only as confirmation.

rules.title: Trade from concepts, not fixed plan
rules.rule: Trade from concepts rather than a rigid step-by-step plan, since every session differs.

sources.statement: You do not need to follow a fixed step-by-step trading plan; trade from concepts because every session is different.

rules.title: Trail stop to breakeven early
rules.rule: Protect the downside by trailing the stop to entry or taking partial profits early.

sources.statement: Your first responsibility is protecting the downside; trail the stop to entry (accounting for spread/commission) or take partials early.

rules.title: Two types of bear bottoms
rules.rule: Distinguish stimulus-rescued crash bottoms from slow exhaustion bottoms when the Fed is constrained.

sources.statement: Bear markets bottom either by a quick 'car crash' rescued by stimulus or by slow 'exhaustion' when the Fed's hands are tied by inflation.

rules.title: Underweight politically risky markets
rules.rule: Underweight markets with high political or intervention uncertainty.

sources.statement: Underweight markets with high political/intervention uncertainty (e.g., China).

rules.title: Use negative balance protection
rules.rule: Use brokers with negative balance protection for leveraged CFDs.

sources.statement: Use brokers with negative balance protection when trading leveraged CFDs/spread bets.

rules.title: Use real executed-trade data
rules.rule: Verify your data is real exchange execution data before trusting models.

sources.statement: Validate that your data is real executed-order data (not CFD tick data) before trusting any model.

rules.title: VIX above Bollinger study
rules.rule: Study asset returns after VIX/VixFix closes above its upper Bollinger Band.

sources.statement: Context: study asset returns after VIX/VixFix closes above an upper Bollinger Band.

rules.title: VIX trendline break marks bottom
rules.rule: Treat a VIX ascending trendline breakdown as a short-term equity bottom.

sources.statement: Paid source: statement withheld.

rules.title: Vertical or BWB with clear target
rules.rule: In a trending market with a clear target, use a vertical call spread or broken-wing butterfly capped at the target.

sources.statement: [Imre Gams] In a trending/one-time-framing market with a clear target (e.g., an untested prior-session POC), use a vertical call spread or broken-wing butterfly since capping upside at the target costs little.
Use a call debit spread on breakouts to define downside while targeting about 5 to 1 reward to risk.

rules.title: Volatility is opportunity
rules.rule: Treat volatility as opportunity rather than threat.

sources.statement: Paid source: statement withheld.
Use event-driven volatility as the entry: volatility shakes people out and that is where the good prices are.

rules.title: Weak Treasury auctions hurt growth
rules.rule: Treat weak Treasury auctions as a yield-lifting headwind for growth stocks.

sources.statement: Use Treasury auction results and foreign demand to judge bond direction and the market's growth and inflation expectations.
Weak Treasury auctions tend to lift yields and act as a headwind for growth stocks.

rules.title: Weekend watchlist preparation
rules.rule: Use weekends to scan markets and build the next week's watchlist.

sources.statement: Prepare on the weekend: map the week's data releases, pick one to three high-quality trades and set alerts.
Use weekends, when markets are closed, to scan and build the next week's watchlist.

rules.title: 10/20-day MA bear cross on QQQ and sector ETFs
rules.rule: Watch for the 10-day moving average crossing below the 20-day on QQQ and leading sector ETFs as confirmation that momentum is deteriorating.

sources.statement: Watch for the 10-day moving average crossing below the 20-day on QQQ and leading sector ETFs as confirmation that momentum is deteriorating.

rules.title: Avoid overnight swings when VIX and gaps are large
rules.rule: Avoid overnight swing trades when the VIX is elevated and gaps are large.

sources.statement: Avoid overnight swing trades when the VIX is elevated and gaps are large.

rules.title: Be biggest at the start and add fast when right
rules.rule: Be bigger at the start of a good trade and add quickly when you are right.

sources.statement: Be bigger at the start of a good trade and add quickly when you are right.

rules.title: Short failed rallies into the 50-day MA
rules.rule: Short a daily rally into the 50-day moving average that fails to reclaim it after a breakdown.

sources.statement: Short a daily rally into the 50-day moving average that fails to reclaim it after a breakdown.

rules.title: Covered call strike at or above price target
rules.rule: Place covered calls at a strike no lower than your price target.

sources.statement: Place covered calls at a strike no lower than your price target.

rules.title: When in doubt, get out
rules.rule: When in doubt, get out of the position and reassess; you can always get back in.

sources.statement: When in doubt, get out of the position and reassess; you can always get back in.
If you are unsure whether to sell after an exhausted move, sell about half and buy back if it drops.

rules.title: Push size only with defined max loss
rules.rule: Push size only when you have a clear stop or a defined max loss such as an option structure.

sources.statement: Push size only when you have a clear stop or a defined max loss such as an option structure.

rules.title: Breakouts need volume and RVOL confirmation
rules.rule: Only take breakout trades when volume confirms the break and relative volume is elevated; exit if volume does not confirm.

sources.statement: Only take breakout trades when volume confirms the break and relative volume is elevated; exit if volume does not confirm.
Confirm price action with volume, giving more weight to high-volume moves.

rules.title: Exit move-to-move trades on 21 EMA close
rules.rule: Exit a move-to-move trade when price closes below a trailing 21 EMA for a long (above for a short), or when an accelerated trendline breaks.

sources.statement: Exit a move-to-move trade when price closes below a trailing 21 EMA for a long (above for a short), or when an accelerated trendline breaks.

rules.title: Exit trend trades at first counter swing
rules.rule: Exit a trend trade at the first higher low in a downtrend or first lower high in an uptrend.

sources.statement: Exit a trend trade at the first higher low in a downtrend or first lower high in an uptrend.

rules.title: Buy tight pullbacks to short-term SMAs in strong stocks
rules.rule: For trend swings, buy a strong stock after it pulls back and tightens near the 5, 10 and 20-day SMAs, entering when it reclaims the 10-day SMA and trailing the stop under the prior day's low.

sources.statement: For trend swings, buy a strong stock after it pulls back and tightens near the 5, 10 and 20-day SMAs, entering when it reclaims the 10-day SMA and trailing the stop under the prior day's low.

rules.title: Keep risk small while new
rules.rule: Keep risk small while you are new, because you are at your least skilled now.

sources.statement: Keep risk small while you are new, because you are at your least skilled now.
Do not trade leverage or go below the four-hour timeframe until the basics are mastered.

rules.title: Manage a trade on its entry timeframe
rules.rule: Enter, exit, and manage a trade on the same time frame.

sources.statement: Enter, exit, and manage a trade on the same time frame.

rules.title: Trade new strategies tiny for the first 20 reps
rules.rule: Trade a new strategy live very small for the first 20 tagged reps before scaling up.

sources.statement: Trade a new strategy live very small for the first 20 tagged reps before scaling up.

rules.title: Roll LEAPS up at 0.9+ delta
rules.rule: Roll a LEAP up in strike when its delta reaches about 0.9-0.95, since its leverage has shrunk.

sources.statement: Roll a LEAP up in strike when liquidity at its deep in-the-money strike starts drying up as the stock rises.
Roll a LEAP up in strike when its delta reaches about 0.9-0.95, since its leverage has shrunk.

rules.title: Buy ITM options for a low break-even
rules.rule: Buy in-the-money options for a low break-even rather than out-of-the-money options; choose by break-even, not by what you can afford.

sources.statement: Buy in-the-money options for a low break-even rather than out-of-the-money options; choose by break-even, not by what you can afford.

rules.title: Sell options back; do not exercise early
rules.rule: Close options by selling them back to the market rather than exercising them early, to keep the extrinsic value.

sources.statement: Close options by selling them back to the market rather than exercising them early, to keep the extrinsic value.

rules.title: Understand assignment before selling options
rules.rule: Learn how assignment and the strategy's profit-and-loss math work before trading spreads or selling options.

sources.statement: Learn how assignment and the strategy's profit-and-loss math work before trading spreads or selling options.

rules.title: Sell premium 30-45 DTE near 0.3 delta
rules.rule: Sell cash-secured puts and covered calls about 30-45 days to expiration, starting near 0.3 delta.

sources.statement: Sell cash-secured puts and covered calls about 30-45 days to expiration, starting near 0.3 delta.

rules.title: Covered calls above cost basis after assignment
rules.rule: After put assignment, sell covered calls above your adjusted cost basis.

sources.statement: After put assignment, write calls above your cost basis until the shares are called away (the wheel).
After put assignment, sell covered calls above your adjusted cost basis.

rules.title: Roll only when credit/collateral return justifies it
rules.rule: Keep rolling a short put only while credit divided by collateral gives an acceptable return for the time locked up.

sources.statement: Keep rolling a short put only while credit divided by collateral gives an acceptable return for the time locked up.

rules.title: PMCC: ~0.7-delta long, ~0.3-delta short 30-45 DTE
rules.rule: For a poor man's covered call, buy the long call in the money near 0.7 delta at least three months out and sell the short call near 0.3 delta 30-45 days out.

sources.statement: For a poor man's covered call, buy the long call in the money near 0.7 delta at least three months out and sell the short call near 0.3 delta 30-45 days out.

rules.title: Long-dated debit call spread: ~0.6-delta long leg
rules.rule: For a long-dated debit call spread, buy the long leg near 0.6 delta about a year out on a liquid underlying and sell the short leg at or out of the money.

sources.statement: For a long-dated debit call spread, buy the long leg near 0.6 delta about a year out on a liquid underlying and sell the short leg at or out of the money.

rules.title: Scale spreads by width, not count
rules.rule: Scale a spread's risk and reward by widening the strikes rather than opening many spreads.

sources.statement: Scale a spread's risk and reward by widening the strikes rather than opening many spreads.

rules.title: Small accounts: avoid high-probability credit spreads
rules.rule: With a small account, avoid high-probability credit spreads whose max loss dwarfs the credit.

sources.statement: With a small account, avoid high-probability credit spreads whose max loss dwarfs the credit.

rules.title: Do not hold options through a stock split
rules.rule: Avoid holding options through a stock split, because the adjusted contracts become illiquid.

sources.statement: Avoid holding options through a stock split, because the adjusted contracts become illiquid.

rules.title: LEAPS over futures for long-term leverage
rules.rule: Use LEAPS rather than futures for long-term leveraged holds, because of convergence and contango.

sources.statement: Use LEAPS rather than futures for long-term leveraged holds, because of convergence and contango.

rules.title: Use far-dated call spreads when a LEAP breaks the cap
rules.rule: If a LEAP would exceed 10% of the portfolio, use a far-dated debit call spread instead.

sources.statement: If a LEAP would exceed 10% of the portfolio, use a far-dated debit call spread instead.

rules.title: Don't invest money needed within a year
rules.rule: Do not invest money you will need within about a year.

sources.statement: Do not invest money you will need within about a year.

rules.title: Minimum account size before options
rules.rule: Wait until the account reaches about $1,000-$1,500 before trading options; grow a small account with shares first.

sources.statement: Wait until the account reaches about $1,000-$1,500 before trading options; grow a small account with shares first.

rules.title: Be able to survive a 50% market drop
rules.rule: Keep your exposure such that you could handle a 50% drop in the stock market.

sources.statement: Stress-test positions and, if the loss would derail your plan, reduce size before adding more.
Keep your exposure such that you could handle a 50% drop in the stock market.
Size crypto (majors only, about 5-10% of the portfolio) so a 50% drawdown does not change your life.
Test risk tolerance in dollars: picture the account down 35% and classify yourself by whether you would buy, hold or sell.

rules.title: Don't buy just under tested resistance
rules.rule: Do not buy right below a resistance level that price has already hit twice.

sources.statement: Do not buy right below a resistance level that price has already hit twice.

rules.title: Buy channel bottom, sell top or middle
rules.rule: In a price channel, buy near the bottom and sell near the top or middle.

sources.statement: In a price channel, buy near the bottom and sell near the top or middle.
In a range, buy the floor or wait for the ceiling to break; do not buy the middle of the range.

rules.title: Time in the market beats timing it
rules.rule: Time in the market beats timing the market.

sources.statement: Stay invested through volatility so you do not miss the bull cycles.
Time in the market beats timing the market.
Once the portfolio is built, review it on a schedule and never in a panic.

rules.title: Buy companies you know and use
rules.rule: Invest in companies whose products you use or would use, that are profitable or close to it, and that are not obscure penny stocks.

sources.statement: Invest in companies whose products you use or would use, that are profitable or close to it, and that are not obscure penny stocks.
Only buy businesses whose way of making money you can explain in one sentence.

rules.title: Buy the story only when fundamentals back it
rules.rule: Use a company's story as a reason to buy only when the fundamentals support it.

sources.statement: Before buying an acquisition story, check the premium, new debt and interest, dilution, and when synergies become cash flow.
Use a company's story as a reason to buy only when the fundamentals support it.
Before buying an IPO, check who is selling, where proceeds go, the tradable float and the implied valuation (price times total shares).
Before buying a turnaround, check when savings arrive, what execution costs and how much becomes sustainable cash flow; wait for evidence.

rules.title: Check cash runway against the thesis horizon
rules.rule: Check the company's cash runway: it must survive long enough for the thesis to play out.

sources.statement: For leveraged spread businesses such as neoclouds, check who the customers are and how growth is funded; reliance on converts and share sales is a yellow flag.
Check the company's cash runway: it must survive long enough for the thesis to play out.
Prefer an IPO priced lower with a large cash raise over a high valuation with a small raise, which risks a later down round.

rules.title: Market cap near cash can be a buy
rules.rule: A stock whose market cap roughly equals its cash on hand is pricing in no future and can be a buy.

sources.statement: A stock whose market cap roughly equals its cash on hand is pricing in no future and can be a buy.

rules.title: Wait quarters after a fraud short report
rules.rule: When a short report alleges inflated earnings, wait a few quarters for confirmation before buying.

sources.statement: When a short report alleges inflated earnings, wait a few quarters for confirmation before buying.

rules.title: Read the FOMC projections, not just the decision
rules.rule: Watch the FOMC economic projections and the projected rate path, not just the rate decision.

sources.statement: When a central bank decision is fully priced, trade its forward guidance words rather than the number.
Watch the FOMC economic projections and the projected rate path, not just the rate decision.
At FOMC and BoJ meetings, watch the guidance and what the chair says (for example about oil) rather than the priced-in rate decision.
When a hike is mostly priced in, watch the guidance and the currency move, not the decision.

rules.title: Don't buy at the IPO; wait
rules.rule: Do not rush to buy at an IPO; wait and see how it trades.

sources.statement: Do not buy a hyped IPO on day one or at the open; retail tends to be the exit liquidity for early investors.
Do not rush to buy at an IPO; wait and see how it trades.
Wait for the post-IPO drawdown and the lockup expiry before buying a hot new listing.

rules.title: Prefer reinvestors over dividend payers
rules.rule: Prefer companies that reinvest earnings in growth over dividend payers.

sources.statement: Prefer companies that reinvest earnings in growth over dividend payers.

rules.title: Hold a year+ for long-term capital gains
rules.rule: Hold winners a year or more to get the long-term capital gains tax rate.

sources.statement: Hold winners a year or more to get the long-term capital gains tax rate.

rules.title: Keep a standing cash reserve as dry powder
rules.rule: Keep a standing cash sleeve (at least about 10%) as dry powder so you can buy when quality assets go on sale instead of being forced to sell.

sources.statement: Keep at least 10% of the portfolio in cash at all times, next to a core of long-term holdings and a swing-trade sleeve.
Keep cash on the side as dry powder so you can buy when great businesses go on sale instead of being forced to sell.
Holding cash or staying flat in a falling year is a position; boring often wins.

rules.title: Small in pullbacks, size up when momentum returns
rules.rule: Keep positions small and protect capital during pullbacks; deploy heavily only when momentum returns and the market breaks higher.

sources.statement: Keep positions small during pullbacks and sit on your hands; deploy heavily only when momentum returns and the market breaks higher.

rules.title: Weight by how real the cash flows are
rules.rule: Put the biggest weights where cash flows already exist and the smallest where there is only a story.

sources.statement: Put the biggest weights where cash flows already exist and the smallest where there is only a story so far.

rules.title: Hedge longs with a short instead of selling
rules.rule: Hedge long holdings with a short on a correlated index or risk asset, or offsetting positions, instead of selling the core.

sources.statement: Hedge long holdings with a short on a correlated index or risk asset (such as the Nasdaq or bitcoin) instead of selling them.
Hedge the book with positions that profit under different outcomes, such as short tech plus long oil, instead of praying.

rules.title: Core, swing and tactical sleeves
rules.rule: Split the book into core, swing and tactical sleeves; only the small tactical sleeve reacts to headline weeks.

sources.statement: Keep intraday trading, swing trading and the long-term portfolio separate.
Let the swing book wait for confirmation; only a small tactical sleeve reacts to headline weeks.

rules.title: Position on peer and customer read-throughs
rules.rule: Use peer and customer earnings, capex and leader commentary as a read-through to position before a related company reports.

sources.statement: Use a peer's or customer's earnings as a read-through to position in a similar company before it reports.
Look for demand signals in customer capex one step above the company in the supply chain.
Use an industry-leading CEO's comments about where demand is heading to find second-order plays.

rules.title: Avoid hyped IPOs at extreme sales multiples
rules.rule: Avoid hyped IPOs at extreme revenue multiples backed by underwriter research; retail is the exit liquidity.

sources.statement: Avoid hyped IPOs at extreme revenue multiples backed by underwriter research; retail is the exit liquidity.

rules.title: Mega-IPO clusters are a top signal
rules.rule: Treat clusters of mega IPOs as a top signal and expect other stocks to bleed as money is freed for them.

sources.statement: Treat clusters of mega IPOs as a top signal, and expect broader stocks to bleed as funds sell to free cash for a mega listing.

rules.title: Play hyped listings through proxies
rules.rule: Play a hyped listing through listed peers, proxies or large shareholders instead of paying the listing-day premium.

sources.statement: Play a hyped listing through listed proxies and peers that get repriced, rather than paying the listing-day premium.

rules.title: Read core CPI, not the headline
rules.rule: On CPI day, react to core inflation rather than the oil-driven headline number.

sources.statement: On CPI day, react to core inflation, not the headline, since oil pushes the headline around.

rules.title: When good news gets sold, sellers control
rules.rule: When strong earnings fail to hold a bid into the close, assume sellers are in control and protect capital.

sources.statement: When a currency sells off despite strong data, read it as inherent weakness.
When the best news of the month gets sold, assume sellers are in control and protect capital.
Judge an earnings reaction by whether price holds into the close, not by the headline.

rules.title: Buy ahead of index inclusion flows
rules.rule: Buy names on a path to major index inclusion or a US listing before the forced passive buying arrives.

sources.statement: Buy names on a path to major index inclusion or a US listing before the forced passive buying arrives.

rules.title: Let mechanical flows clear before buying
rules.rule: When a dip or discount comes from index or rebalancing flows rather than the business, let the flows clear and then buy.

sources.statement: Do not buy a dip driven by dealer hedging and systematic flows until the large options expiry has passed.
When a dip or discount comes from mechanical index or rebalancing flows rather than the business, let the flows clear and then buy.

rules.title: Follow government stakes and funding
rules.rule: Favor companies and sectors with direct government equity stakes, backing or multi-year funding commitments.

sources.statement: Favor companies and sectors with direct government equity stakes or multi-year government funding.

rules.title: Industry-leader adoption as a signal
rules.rule: Treat an industry leader adopting, investing in or partnering with a company as a strong signal.

sources.statement: Treat an industry leader such as Nvidia adopting, investing in or partnering with a company as a strong signal.

rules.title: Pick the industry tailwind before the company
rules.rule: Start with an industry that has a tailwind; underwrite the pie growing rather than one company winning outright.

sources.statement: Start with an industry that has a tailwind before picking the company; a mediocre company in a growing industry beats a great one in a dying industry.
For a share-losing leader in a fast-growing market, underwrite the market growing faster than the share shrinks rather than outright victory.

rules.title: Moat test: switching costs, pricing power, data
rules.rule: Favor companies with a real moat: customers would suffer without them, high switching costs, or proprietary data.

sources.statement: Favor companies with a real moat and pricing power: test whether customers would actually suffer if the company disappeared, and look for high switching costs.
Favor businesses with high switching costs, where customers do not rip you out once they build you in.
Favor companies that own proprietary data the AI era depends on.

rules.title: Accelerating revenue, raised guidance, expanding margins
rules.rule: Favor businesses with accelerating revenue, raised guidance, booked demand and revenue growing faster than costs.

sources.statement: Favor leaders with accelerating revenue, raised guidance and booked deals that lock in demand.
Favor businesses whose revenue grows faster than costs so margins expand.

rules.title: Cyclicals with multi-year contracted minimums
rules.rule: In cyclical sectors, favor companies with multi-year contracts, committed volumes and guaranteed minimums.

sources.statement: In cyclical sectors, favor companies that lock in multi-year contracts with committed volumes and guaranteed minimums.

rules.title: Smallest name or proxy for most torque
rules.rule: Within a theme, prefer the smallest company or lower-cap proxies with leverage to the underlying for the most upside.

sources.statement: Within a theme, prefer the smallest company or lower-cap proxies with leverage to the underlying for the most upside torque.

rules.title: Toll-booth businesses that win either way
rules.rule: Favor businesses that take a fee on every transaction or win no matter which competitor wins.

sources.statement: Favor toll-booth businesses that take a fee on every transaction and earn whether the market goes up or down.
Favor businesses that win no matter which competitor wins, such as royalty or licensing models.

rules.title: Judge pre-revenue names on pipeline
rules.rule: For pre-revenue qualification-cycle companies, judge on pipeline growth rather than trailing revenue.

sources.statement: For pre-revenue qualification-cycle companies, judge on pipeline growth rather than trailing revenue.

rules.title: Index level from forward EPS x normal multiple
rules.rule: Value the index as forward earnings times a normal multiple (about 20x) to judge its fair level.

sources.statement: Value the index as forward earnings times a normal multiple (about 20x) to judge where it can go.

rules.title: Cyclicals look cheapest at the top
rules.rule: Do not buy cyclicals because they look cheap at peak earnings; they usually top months before earnings peak.

sources.statement: Do not buy cyclicals because they look cheap: they look cheapest at the top and usually peak months before peak earnings.

rules.title: Judge what the price already expects
rules.rule: Separate the business from the stock: judge valuation by the expectations already baked into the price.

sources.statement: Before buying good news, ask how much optimism is already in the price; before buying weakness, ask what bad news is priced in.
Separate the strength of the business from whether the stock price already reflects it.
Judge valuation by the expectations baked into the price, not whether the P/E looks high.

rules.title: Rotate into cheap laggards; wait for capital to return
rules.rule: Rotate toward quality names and sectors that never ran and stayed cheap, and buy a sector's dip once capital rotates back in.

sources.statement: Rotate into quality businesses and sectors the crowd ignored and left cheap while it chases an overvalued hot theme.
Among peers, prefer the cheapest one that has not run yet over the one that already ran.
Wait for capital to rotate back into a sector before buying its dip, even if its fundamentals are strong.
When beaten-down names start beating and raising, read it as money rotating in.

rules.title: Yen and JGB yields as early warning
rules.rule: Watch the yen and Japanese government bond yields as an early warning for carry unwinds and higher US yields.

sources.statement: When a funding currency like the yen strengthens fast, expect forced sellers to sell the winners, such as tech; tech holders should watch USD/JPY.
Watch the yen and Japanese government bond yields as an early warning for carry unwinds that lift US yields.

rules.title: Oil leads geopolitical outcomes
rules.rule: Use the oil price, not headlines, as the leading indicator of geopolitical deal outcomes.

sources.statement: Use oil, not tweets or headlines, as the leading indicator of geopolitical deal outcomes.

rules.title: A ceasefire is not a resolution
rules.rule: Do not treat a geopolitical pause or ceasefire as a resolution; expect oil spikes to return.

sources.statement: Do not confuse a ceasefire or pause with a resolution; expect oil spikes to return and do not assume the oil trade is over.

rules.title: Markets test a new Fed chair
rules.rule: Expect a pullback of about 10% around a Fed chair transition and do not rush to buy ahead of it.

sources.statement: Expect markets to test a new Fed chair with a pullback of about 10%, and do not rush to buy ahead of the transition.

rules.title: Draw ranges at the wicks
rules.rule: Draw range highs and lows at the wicks, not the candle bodies.

sources.statement: Draw ranges including the wicks.

rules.title: Repeated wicks at highs signal exhaustion
rules.rule: Treat repeated wicks at the highs and rounding tops as exhaustion of the move.

sources.statement: Treat repeated wicks at the highs and rounding tops as exhaustion: sellers keep rejecting the breakout.

rules.title: Never bet more than Kelly
rules.rule: Size bets at or below the Kelly fraction (for even-money bets, the edge), and below full Kelly because the true edge is uncertain; overbetting destroys growth.

sources.statement: Never bet more than the Kelly fraction (for an even-money bet, your edge); betting twice Kelly grows nothing and pushes most players toward ruin.
Size below full Kelly, because real edges are never known exactly and overestimating the edge means overbetting.

rules.title: Volatility forecasts lag sudden crashes
rules.rule: Do not rely on backward-looking volatility forecasts to cut size before a crash that follows a calm stretch; they react only afterward.

sources.statement: Do not count on a volatility forecast to protect you from a crash after a calm stretch; backward-looking forecasts react only after the hit.

rules.title: Drops raise volatility more than rallies
rules.rule: Expect volatility to rise more after a drop than after an equal rally, and treat symmetric volatility models as underestimating risk right after a sell-off.

sources.statement: Expect volatility to rise much more after a drop than after an equal rally, and treat symmetric models as underestimating risk right after a sell-off.

rules.title: Risk parity: equal risk contribution
rules.rule: Weight asset classes so each contributes the same share of portfolio risk (simplest form: inverse-volatility weights) instead of letting stocks dominate a 60/40 mix.

sources.statement: Weight asset classes so each contributes the same share of total risk (simplest form: inverse-volatility weights) instead of a 60/40 mix where stocks carry about 90% of the risk.

rules.title: Anchor allocation on market weights, tilt by view confidence
rules.rule: Start from market-cap weights and tilt toward your own return views only in proportion to your confidence, since small return-estimate errors push optimizer weights to extremes.

sources.statement: Start allocations from market-capitalization weights and tilt toward your own return views only in proportion to your confidence, because small errors in return estimates push optimizer weights to extremes.

rules.title: Prove mean reversion before trading it
rules.rule: Trade mean reversion only in series with a statistically proven pull back (spreads, ratios, rates), using a strict t-statistic limit of about -3 and the half-life.

sources.statement: Trade mean reversion only where a pull back has been proven (spreads, ratios, rates rather than single stock prices), using a stricter t-statistic limit of about -3.

rules.title: Momentum crashes on sharp rebounds
rules.rule: Expect momentum portfolios to suffer sudden large losses when markets turn sharply and past losers rebound.
